translationRepairs: Book of Sui, 44th year of Volume, ninth year of Biographies
Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine
卷四十四列傳第九 is Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine; the idiomatic line wrongly reads 卷/第 as 'year' and invents regnal-style dating that the Chinese does not support.
Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a maternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu by the same mother.
高祖母弟 means Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother, not a maternal cousin; the proposed idiomatic wording restores the kinship correctly.
Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was a younger cousin on Empress Gao's side.
Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother.
高祖母弟 is Gaozu's same-mother younger brother; the literal wrongly takes 高祖 as Empress Gao and 母弟 as cousin on her side.
After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the temple name Xuan.
After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the posthumous name Xuan.
諡曰宣 grants the posthumous name Xuan (諡), not a temple name (廟號); replacing 'temple name' with 'posthumous name' matches the Chinese.
After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the temple name Jing.
After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the posthumous name Jing.
諡曰景 grants the posthumous name Jing (諡), not a temple name (廟號); the proposed replacement is accurate.
